title: Iznik tile painting
summary: Iznik tiles are painted by hand on a white body in cobalt blue, clear turquoise and a raised tomato red. Here you draw a tulip, a carnation and a long saw-edged leaf across a panel of nine tiles, then flood them with glaze.
howToPlay: Look at the small panel at the top: it shows the finished tiles.
Pick cobalt and drag along the lit lines to draw the outlines; press Next when the drawing is done.
Pick a glaze and tap a shape to flood it: tomato red for the tulip and carnation, turquoise for the leaf.
Add the fine cobalt veins, then press Check to see your stars. Mirror repeats each stroke on the other half of the panel.
rules: The panel has three steps in order: outlines, glaze fills, veins.
The brush carries a limited load of paint; dip it again when the line runs dry.
A line scores by how closely it follows the guide; a fill scores by how much of the shape holds the right glaze.
Glaze that spills outside an outline counts against you; undo takes back the last stroke.
With Mirror on, each stroke is repeated on the other half of the panel.
Three stars for a close, clean, well-coloured panel.
heritageNote: Iznik, the old town of Nicaea in north-west Turkey, was the centre of a famous tile and pottery industry from the late fifteenth to the seventeenth century. Its quartz-rich white body, cobalt, turquoise and raised red glazes decorated palaces and public buildings across the Ottoman world, and potters in Iznik and Kutahya keep the craft alive today.
